title: Measurement: Tavily is probed only after its own approval, a failed probe changes nothing, and the research choice writer clears its grant
summary: TSK-0035, toward ACC-0054, as COMPONENT PROOF ONLY. The implementation is commit 7115a56, and the sha256 of each file is in the facts. lib/research-enablement.mjs adds the Tavily step of setup and the research choice writer. lib/consent-record.mjs gains reconcileGrant and peekGrant, which judge one choice-keyed grant by its own choice so that the research step, which does not know the model selection, cannot clear a model-use grant. THE STEP. Inspection's presence result decides whether anything is asked. Absent gives no-credential and not-inspected gives user-disabled, and neither asks, reads the key or writes. With the key present, the separate approval uses the section 6.5 prompt verbatim, or --research tavily stands in for it. The first read of the key is the adapter's GET /usage probe, after the answer. Only an available probe persists anything: the project choice tavily in .pi/kiln.json through the setup transaction, and this host's grant in the consent record. The decision is made with peekGrant, which changes nothing, so a stale grant (a Tavily grant beside a project with no research choice) stands as ask and needs fresh approval, but is removed only by a successful enablement. A decline is persisted: a project with no choice takes none, and a project where another operator committed tavily keeps it while this host's decline is recorded. A non-boolean answer grants nothing and writes nothing. Every path returns an outcome, so declining never blocks planning. OUTCOMES. available, no-credential, authentication-failed, quota-exhausted, backend-unreachable and user-disabled carry the section 6.5 wording, with remaining credits only when Tavily reports them. Every user-disabled result carries a hint naming --research tavily. THE WRITER. writeResearchChoice clears this host's research grant before writing the choice, so a crash between the two leaves the old choice with no grant, which only asks again. Disabling always succeeds: when the grant cannot be cleared (Git cannot verify the record, or it is tracked), the write to none still goes ahead and reports the grant as uncleared. Every write back to tavily requires a successful clear first and is refused without one, with the reason in plain English. HOW IT IS OBSERVED. The real createTavilyAdapter is given an environment Proxy that counts reads of TAVILY_API_KEY and a fetch that records every request and answers as Tavily would. Counts are taken at the prompt. RESULTS. (1) Approval before use: zero key reads and zero requests at the prompt, then exactly one GET /usage (the positive control), available with 988 of 1000 credits, tavily committed and the grant recorded. An unchanged rerun asks nothing and probes again. (2) Failed probes: 401, 403, 429, 432, zero credits, a network error, a 500 and the key gone each give their own outcome and write neither file. (3) STALE GRANT (D4): with no research choice and a stale Tavily grant, approval is asked with zero key use at the prompt, and after a 401, a 429 and a network error both kiln.json and the consent record are byte-identical. The absent and not-inspected paths also leave the record byte-identical, and a successful probe then replaces the grant. (4) ROUND TRIP: tavily to none through the writer removes the grant, none to tavily through the writer revives nothing, and the next setup asks with zero key use at the prompt. (5) Clear before write: a concurrent edit that makes the merge refuse still leaves the grant cleared and the choice unchanged. (6) D1, WITH GIT UNAVAILABLE AND WITH A TRACKED RECORD: disabling succeeds through the writer and through --research disabled, and the record that cannot be cleared is left byte-identical. Enabling through the writer or --research tavily is refused and changes nothing. Once the record can be cleared (Git available, or the removal committed), enabling clears the old grant first and the next setup asks. (7) Declines are remembered in both scopes, --research disabled writes none without reading the key, and neither file holds the key. (8) A research-only reconcile leaves the model-use grant in place. LIMITS. After a disable that could not clear the grant, the grant stays in the record until a later Kiln write to tavily clears it. A change back to tavily made outside Kiln, such as a checkout, once the record is trusted again is not seen by the writer, and a read that sees the tavily choice would then find the grant. That is the observation limit recorded in EVD-0126. The model selection writer (TSK-0036) and the launch path are not connected, so ACC-0054 is not evaluated here. Making the key available only to the research child, parsing --research and placing the step in setup (TSK-0060) are not part of this, and the setup help must name --research tavily when that command exists. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Eight changes each failed the tests: no clear in the writer, the clear after the write, the probe before the answer, persisting before the probe, a truthy answer as approval, disabling refused without a clear, enabling allowed without a clear, and clearing before the probe. Each was restored byte-identical by sha256. CI had not run on 7115a56 when this was recorded, and its result is added separately.

facts.tests: test/research-enablement.test.mjs 14 tests; with test/consent-record.test.mjs and test/connection-inspection.test.mjs, 38 pass, 0 fail
facts.observation: real createTavilyAdapter; environment Proxy counting TAVILY_API_KEY reads; fetch recording every request; counts taken at the prompt
facts.approval-before-use: zero key reads and zero requests at the prompt; then exactly GET https://api.tavily.com/usage; available, 988 of 1000 credits; unchanged rerun asks nothing
facts.failed-probes: 401, 403, 429, 432, zero credits, network error, 500, key gone: distinct outcomes, neither file written
facts.d4-stale-grant: no research choice plus a stale Tavily grant: approval asked with zero key use; after 401, 429 and a network error both files byte-identical; absent and not-inspected leave the record byte-identical; a successful probe replaces the grant
facts.round-trip: tavily to none through the writer removes the grant; none to tavily revives nothing; the next setup asks with zero key use at the prompt
facts.clear-before-write: a concurrent-edit refusal of the merge leaves the grant cleared and the choice unchanged
facts.d1-git-unavailable: disable succeeds (writer and --research disabled), record byte-identical, reported uncleared; enable refused and changes nothing; with Git available, enable clears the old grant and the next setup asks
facts.d1-tracked-record: same sequence with the record force-added; enabling succeeds only after the removal is committed
facts.d2-declines: no choice yet: decline commits none; committed tavily: only this host's decline is recorded and the choice is kept
facts.d3-hint: every user-disabled result carries: To enable web research later, run setup again with --research tavily.
facts.wording: the six outcomes and the approval prompt match section 6.5 of docs/agent-delivery-technical-proposal.md
facts.no-credential-in-files: neither .pi/kiln.json nor the consent record contains the key
facts.model-grant-untouched: a research-only reconcile leaves the model-use grant in place
facts.mutations: 8 of 8 killed locally on Windows, each restored byte-identical by sha256
facts.full-suite-local: npm test on Windows: 1489 tests, 1484 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped

omissions.reason: The model selection writer (TSK-0036) and the launch path are not connected. This is component proof, and ACC-0054 is evaluated once those are.
CI had not run on 7115a56 when this was recorded. Only local Windows results are recorded here, and the CI result is added separately.
The probe ran against a recorded fetch that answers as Tavily would. No request reached Tavily.
Making the key available only to the research child is outside this task.
Parsing --research and placing the step in setup belong to TSK-0060, whose help text must name --research tavily.
